18159.text: And he proceeded to call out like a lion: “Upon the watchtower, O Jehovah, I am standing constantly by day, and at my guardpost I am stationed all the nights.

18160.label: Isaiah 21:9
18160.text: And here, now, there is coming a war chariot of men, [with] a span of steeds!” And he began to speak up and say: “She has fallen! Babylon has fallen, and all the graven images of her gods he has broken to the earth!”

18161.label: Isaiah 21:10
18161.text: O my threshed ones and the son of my threshing floor, what I have heard from Jehovah of armies, the God of Israel, I have reported to YOU people.

18162.label: Isaiah 21:11
18162.text: The pronouncement against Duʹmah: To me there is one calling out from Seʹir: “Watchman, what about the night? Watchman, what about the night?”

18163.label: Isaiah 21:12
18163.text: The watchman said: “The morning has to come, and also the night. If YOU people would inquire, inquire. Come again!”

18164.label: Isaiah 21:13
18164.text: The pronouncement against the desert plain: In the forest in the desert plain YOU will spend the night, O caravans of men of Deʹdan.

18165.label: Isaiah 21:14
18165.text: To meet the thirsty one BRING water. O YOU inhabitants of the land of Teʹma, confront the one fleeing away with bread for him.

18166.label: Isaiah 21:15
18166.text: For because of the swords they have fled away, because of the drawn sword, and because of the bent bow and because of the heaviness of the war.

18167.label: Isaiah 21:16
18167.text: For this is what Jehovah has said to me: “Within yet a year, according to the years of a hired laborer, all the glory of Keʹdar must even come to its end.

18168.label: Isaiah 21:17
18168.text: And the ones remaining over of the number of bow[men], the mighty men of the sons of Keʹdar, will become few, for Jehovah himself, the God of Israel, has spoken [it].”

18169.label: Isaiah 22:1
18169.text: The pronouncement of the valley of the vision: What is the matter with you, then, that you have gone up in your entirety to the roofs?

18170.label: Isaiah 22:2
18170.text: With turmoil you were full, a boisterous city, an exultant town. Your slain ones are not those slain with the sword, nor those dead in battle.

18171.label: Isaiah 22:3
18171.text: All your dictators themselves have fled at one time. Without [need of] a bow they have been taken prisoner. All those of you who have been found have been taken prisoner together. Far off they had run away.

18172.label: Isaiah 22:4
18172.text: That is why I have said: “Turn YOUR gaze away from me. I will show bitterness in weeping. Do not YOU people insist on comforting me over the despoiling of the daughter of my people.

18173.label: Isaiah 22:5
18173.text: For it is the day of confusion and of downtreading and of confounding that the Sovereign Lord, Jehovah of armies, has in the valley of the vision. There is the demolisher of the wall, and the cry to the mountain.

18174.label: Isaiah 22:6
18174.text: And Eʹlam itself has taken up the quiver, in the war chariot of earthling man, [with] steeds; and Kir itself has uncovered the shield.

18175.label: Isaiah 22:7
18175.text: And it will occur that the choicest of your low plains must become full of war chariots, and the very steeds must without fail set themselves in position at the gate,

18176.label: Isaiah 22:8
18176.text: and one will remove the screen of Judah. And you will look in that day toward the armory of the house of the forest,

18177.label: Isaiah 22:9
18177.text: and YOU people will certainly see the very breaches of the City of David, for they will actually be many. And YOU will collect the waters of the lower pool.

18178.label: Isaiah 22:10
18178.text: And the houses of Jerusalem YOU will actually count. YOU will also pull down the houses to make the wall unattainable.

18179.label: Isaiah 22:11
18179.text: And there will be a collecting basin that YOU must make between the two walls for the waters of the old pool. And YOU will certainly not look at the grand maker of it, and the one forming it long ago YOU will certainly not see.

18180.label: Isaiah 22:12
18180.text: “And the Sovereign Lord, Jehovah of armies, will call in that day for weeping and for mourning and for baldness and for girding on sackcloth.

18181.label: Isaiah 22:13
18181.text: But, look! exultation and rejoicing, the killing of cattle and the slaughtering of sheep, the eating of flesh and the drinking of wine, ‘Let there be eating and drinking, for tomorrow we shall die.’”

18182.label: Isaiah 22:14
18182.text: And in my ears Jehovah of armies has revealed himself: “‘This error will not be atoned for in YOUR behalf until YOU people die,’ the Sovereign Lord, Jehovah of armies, has said.”

18183.label: Isaiah 22:15
18183.text: This is what the Sovereign Lord, Jehovah of armies, has said: “Go, enter in to this steward, to Shebʹna, who is over the house,

18184.label: Isaiah 22:16
18184.text: ‘What is there of interest to you here, and who is there of interest to you here, that you have hewed out for yourself here a burial place?’ On a height he is hewing out his burial place; in a crag he is cutting out a residence for himself.

18185.label: Isaiah 22:17
18185.text: ‘Look! Jehovah is hurling you down with violent hurling, O able-bodied man, and grasping you forcibly.

18186.label: Isaiah 22:18
18186.text: Without fail he will wrap you up tightly, like a ball for a wide land. There you will die, and there the chariots of your glory will be the dishonor of the house of your master.

18187.label: Isaiah 22:19
18187.text: And I will push you away from your position; and from your official standing one will tear you down.

18188.label: Isaiah 22:20
18188.text: “‘And it must occur in that day that I will call my servant, namely, E·liʹa·kim the son of Hil·kiʹah.

18189.label: Isaiah 22:21
18189.text: And I will clothe him with your robe, and your sash I shall firmly bind about him, and your dominion I shall give into his hand; and he must become a father to the inhabitant of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.

18190.label: Isaiah 22:22
18190.text: And I will put the key of the house of David upon his shoulder, and he must open without anyone’s shutting, and he must shut without anyone’s opening.

18191.label: Isaiah 22:23
18191.text: And I will drive him in as a peg in a lasting place, and he must become as a throne of glory to the house of his father.

18192.label: Isaiah 22:24
18192.text: And they must hang upon him all the glory of the house of his father, the descendants and the offshoots, all the vessels of the small sort, the vessels of the bowl sort as well as all the vessels of the large jars.

18193.label: Isaiah 22:25
18193.text: “‘In that day,’ is the utterance of Jehovah of armies, ‘the peg that is driven in a lasting place will be removed, and it must be hewn down and fall, and the load that is upon it must be cut off, for Jehovah himself has spoken [it].’”

18194.label: Isaiah 23:1
18194.text: The pronouncement of Tyre: Howl, YOU ships of Tarʹshish! for it has been despoiled from [being] a port, from [being a place] to enter in. From the land of Kitʹtim it has been revealed to them.

18195.label: Isaiah 23:2
18195.text: Be silent, YOU inhabitants of the coastland. The merchants from Siʹdon, the ones crossing over the sea—they have filled you.

18196.label: Isaiah 23:3
18196.text: And on many waters has been the seed of Shiʹhor, the harvest of the Nile, her revenue; and it came to be the profit of the nations.

18197.label: Isaiah 23:4
18197.text: Be ashamed, O Siʹdon; because the sea, O you stronghold of the sea, has said: “I have not had birth pains, and I have not given birth, nor have I brought up young men, raised up virgins.”

18198.label: Isaiah 23:5
18198.text: Just as at the report pertaining to Egypt, people will likewise be in severe pains at the report on Tyre.

18199.label: Isaiah 23:6
18199.text: Cross over to Tarʹshish; howl, YOU inhabitants of the coastland.

18200.label: Isaiah 23:7
18200.text: Is this YOUR [city] that was exultant from days of long ago, [from] her early times? Her feet used to bring her far away to reside as an alien.

18201.label: Isaiah 23:8
18201.text: Who is it that has given this counsel against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, whose merchants were princes, whose tradesmen were the honorable ones of the earth?

18202.label: Isaiah 23:9
18202.text: Jehovah of armies himself has given this counsel, to profane the pride of all beauty, to treat with contempt all the honorable ones of the earth.

18203.label: Isaiah 23:10
18203.text: Cross over your land like the Nile River, O daughter of Tarʹshish. There is no shipyard any longer.

18204.label: Isaiah 23:11
18204.text: His hand he has stretched out over the sea; he has caused kingdoms to be agitated. Jehovah himself has given a command against Phoe·niʹcia, to annihilate her strongholds.

18205.label: Isaiah 23:12
18205.text: And he says: “You must never again exult, O oppressed one, the virgin daughter of Siʹdon. Get up, cross over to Kitʹtim itself. Even there it will not be restful for you.”

18206.label: Isaiah 23:13
18206.text: Look! The land of the Chal·deʹans. This is the people—As·syrʹi·a did not prove to be [the one]—they founded her for the desert haunters. They have erected their siege towers; they have stripped bare her dwelling towers; one has set her as a crumbling ruin.

18207.label: Isaiah 23:14
18207.text: Howl, YOU ships of Tarʹshish, for YOUR stronghold has been despoiled.

18208.label: Isaiah 23:15
18208.text: And it must occur in that day that Tyre must be forgotten seventy years, the same as the days of one king. At the end of seventy years it will happen to Tyre as in the song of a prostitute:

18209.label: Isaiah 23:16
18209.text: “Take a harp, go around the city, O forgotten prostitute. Do your best at playing on the strings; make your songs many, in order that you may be remembered.”

18210.label: Isaiah 23:17
18210.text: And it must occur at the end of seventy years that Jehovah will turn his attention to Tyre, and she must return to her hire and commit prostitution with all the kingdoms of the earth upon the surface of the ground.

18211.label: Isaiah 23:18
18211.text: And her profit and her hire must become something holy to Jehovah. It will not be stored up, nor be laid up, because her hire will come to be for those dwelling before Jehovah, for eating to satisfaction and for elegant covering.

18212.label: Isaiah 24:1
18212.text: Look! Jehovah is emptying the land and laying it waste, and he has twisted the face of it and scattered its inhabitants.

18213.label: Isaiah 24:2
18213.text: And it must come to be the same for the people as for the priest; the same for the servant as for his master; the same for the maidservant as for her mistress; the same for the buyer as for the seller; the same for the lender as for the borrower; the same for the interest taker as for the one paying the interest.

18214.label: Isaiah 24:3
18214.text: Without fail the land will be emptied, and without fail it will be plundered, for Jehovah himself has spoken this word.

18215.label: Isaiah 24:4
18215.text: The land has gone to mourning, has faded away. The productive land has withered, has faded away. The high ones of the people of the land have withered.

18216.label: Isaiah 24:5
18216.text: And the very land has been polluted under its inhabitants, for they have bypassed the laws, changed the regulation, broken the indefinitely lasting covenant.

18217.label: Isaiah 24:6
18217.text: That is why the curse itself has eaten up the land, and those inhabiting it are held guilty. That is why the inhabitants of the land have decreased in number, and very few mortal men have remained over.

18218.label: Isaiah 24:7
18218.text: The new wine has gone to mourning, the vine has withered, all those glad at heart have gone to sighing.

18219.label: Isaiah 24:8
18219.text: The exultation of the tambourines has ceased, the noise of the highly elated ones has discontinued, the exultation of the harp has ceased.

18220.label: Isaiah 24:9
18220.text: It is with no song that they drink wine; the intoxicating liquor becomes bitter to those drinking it.

18221.label: Isaiah 24:10
18221.text: The deserted town has been broken down; every house has been shut up from entering.

18222.label: Isaiah 24:11
18222.text: There is an outcry in the streets for [want of] wine. All rejoicing has passed away; the exultation of the land has departed.

18223.label: Isaiah 24:12
18223.text: In the city an astonishing condition has been left behind; the gate has been crushed to a mere rubble heap.

18224.label: Isaiah 24:13
18224.text: For thus it will become in the midst of the land, in among the peoples, like the beating off of the olive tree, like the gleaning when the grape gathering has come to an end.

18225.label: Isaiah 24:14
18225.text: They themselves will raise their voice, they will cry out joyfully. In the superiority of Jehovah they will certainly cry out shrilly from the sea.

18226.label: Isaiah 24:15
18226.text: That is why in the region of light they must glorify Jehovah, in the islands of the sea the name of Jehovah, the God of Israel.

18227.label: Isaiah 24:16
18227.text: From the extremity of the land there are melodies that we have heard: “Decoration to the Righteous One!” But I say: “For me there is leanness, for me there is leanness! Woe to me! The treacherous dealers have dealt treacherously. Even with treachery the treacherous dealers have dealt treacherously.”

18228.label: Isaiah 24:17
18228.text: Dread and the hollow and the trap are upon you, you inhabitant of the land.

18229.label: Isaiah 24:18
18229.text: And it must occur that anyone fleeing from the sound of the dreaded thing will fall into the hollow, and anyone coming up from inside the hollow will be caught in the trap. For the very floodgates on high will actually be opened, and the foundations of the land will rock.

18230.label: Isaiah 24:19
18230.text: The land has absolutely burst apart, the land has absolutely been shaken up, the land has absolutely been sent staggering.

18231.label: Isaiah 24:20
18231.text: The land absolutely moves unsteadily like a drunken man, and it has swayed to and fro like a lookout hut. And its transgression has become heavy upon it, and it must fall, so that it will not rise up again.

18232.label: Isaiah 24:21
18232.text: And it must occur in that day that Jehovah will turn his attention upon the army of the height in the height, and upon the kings of the ground upon the ground.

18233.label: Isaiah 24:22
18233.text: And they will certainly be gathered with a gathering as of prisoners into the pit, and be shut up in the dungeon; and after an abundance of days they will be given attention.

18234.label: Isaiah 24:23
18234.text: And the full moon has become abashed, and the glowing [sun] has become ashamed, for Jehovah of armies has become king in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem and in front of his elderly men with glory.

18235.label: Isaiah 25:1
18235.text: O Jehovah, you are my God. I exalt you, I laud your name, for you have done wonderful things, counsels from early times, in faithfulness, in trustworthiness.

18236.label: Isaiah 25:2
18236.text: For you have made a city a pile of stones, a fortified town a crumbling ruin, a dwelling tower of strangers to be no city, which will not be rebuilt even to time indefinite.

18237.label: Isaiah 25:3
18237.text: That is why those who are a strong people will glorify you; the town of the tyrannical nations, they will fear you.

18238.label: Isaiah 25:4
18238.text: For you have become a stronghold to the lowly one, a stronghold to the poor one in the distress that he has, a refuge from the rainstorm, a shade from the heat, when the blast of the tyrannical ones is like a rainstorm against a wall.

18239.label: Isaiah 25:5
18239.text: Like the heat in a waterless country, the noise of strangers you subdue, the heat with the shadow of a cloud. The melody itself of the tyrannical ones becomes suppressed.

18240.label: Isaiah 25:6
18240.text: And Jehovah of armies will certainly make for all the peoples, in this mountain, a banquet of well-oiled dishes, a banquet of [wine kept on] the dregs, of well-oiled dishes filled with marrow, of [wine kept on] the dregs, filtered.

18241.label: Isaiah 25:7
18241.text: And in this mountain he will certainly swallow up the face of the envelopment that is enveloping over all the peoples, and the woven work that is interwoven upon all the nations.

18242.label: Isaiah 25:8
18242.text: He will actually swallow up death forever, and the Sovereign Lord Jehovah will certainly wipe the tears from all faces. And the reproach of his people he will take away from all the earth, for Jehovah himself has spoken [it].

18243.label: Isaiah 25:9
18243.text: And in that day one will certainly say: “Look! This is our God. We have hoped in him, and he will save us. This is Jehovah. We have hoped in him. Let us be joyful and rejoice in the salvation by him.”

18244.label: Isaiah 25:10
18244.text: For the hand of Jehovah will settle down on this mountain, and Moʹab must be trodden down in its place as when a straw heap is trodden down in a manure place.

18245.label: Isaiah 25:11
18245.text: And he must slap out his hands in the midst of it as when a swimmer slaps [them] out to swim, and he must abase its haughtiness with the tricky movements of his hands.

18246.label: Isaiah 25:12
18246.text: And the fortified city, with your high walls of security, he must lay low; he must abase [it], bring [it] into contact with the earth, to the dust.

18247.label: Isaiah 26:1
18247.text: In that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: “We have a strong city. He sets salvation itself for walls and rampart.

18248.label: Isaiah 26:2
18248.text: Open the gates, YOU men, that the righteous nation that is keeping faithful conduct may enter.

18249.label: Isaiah 26:3
18249.text: The inclination that is well supported you will safeguard in continuous peace, because it is in you that one is made to trust.

18250.label: Isaiah 26:4
18250.text: Trust in Jehovah, YOU people, for all times, for in Jah Jehovah is the Rock of times indefinite.

18251.label: Isaiah 26:5
18251.text: “For he has laid low those inhabiting the height, the elevated town. He abases it, he abases it to the earth; he brings it in touch with the dust.

18252.label: Isaiah 26:6
18252.text: The foot will trample it down, the feet of the afflicted one, the steps of the lowly ones.”

18253.label: Isaiah 26:7
18253.text: The path of the righteous one is uprightness. You being upright, you will smooth out the very course of a righteous one.

18254.label: Isaiah 26:8
18254.text: Yes, for the path of your judgments, O Jehovah, we have hoped in you. For your name and for your memorial the desire of the soul has been.

18255.label: Isaiah 26:9
18255.text: With my soul I have desired you in the night; yes, with my spirit within me I keep looking for you; because, when there are judgments from you for the earth, righteousness is what the inhabitants of the productive land will certainly learn.

18256.label: Isaiah 26:10
18256.text: Though the wicked one should be shown favor, he simply will not learn righteousness. In the land of straightforwardness he will act unjustly and will not see the eminence of Jehovah.

18257.label: Isaiah 26:11
18257.text: O Jehovah, your hand has become high, [but] they do not behold [it]. They will behold and be ashamed at the zeal for [your] people. Yes, the very fire for your own adversaries will eat them up.

18258.label: Isaiah 26:12
18258.text: O Jehovah, you will adjudge peace to us, because even all our works you have performed for us.

18259.label: Isaiah 26:13
18259.text: O Jehovah our God, other masters besides you have acted as owners of us. By you only shall we make mention of your name.

18260.label: Isaiah 26:14
18260.text: They are dead; they will not live. Impotent in death, they will not rise up. Therefore you have turned your attention that you might annihilate them and destroy all mention of them.

18261.label: Isaiah 26:15
18261.text: You have added to the nation; O Jehovah, you have added to the nation; you have glorified yourself. You have extended afar all the borders of the land.

18262.label: Isaiah 26:16
18262.text: O Jehovah, during distress they have turned their attention to you; they have poured out a whisper [of prayer] when they had your disciplining.

18263.label: Isaiah 26:17
18263.text: Just as a pregnant woman draws near to giving birth, has labor pains, cries out in her birth pangs, so we have become because of you, O Jehovah.

18264.label: Isaiah 26:18
18264.text: We have become pregnant, we have had labor pains; as it were, we have given birth to wind. No real salvation do we accomplish as regards the land, and no inhabitants for the productive land proceed to fall [in birth].

18265.label: Isaiah 26:19
18265.text: “Your dead ones will live. A corpse of mine —they will rise up. Awake and cry out joyfully, YOU residents in the dust! For your dew is as the dew of mallows, and the earth itself will let even those impotent in death drop [in birth].

18266.label: Isaiah 26:20
18266.text: “Go, my people, enter into your interior rooms, and shut your doors behind you. Hide yourself for but a moment until the denunciation passes over.

18267.label: Isaiah 26:21
18267.text: For, look! Jehovah is coming forth from his place to call to account the error of the inhabitant of the land against him, and the land will certainly expose her bloodshed and will no longer cover over her killed ones.”

18268.label: Isaiah 27:1
18268.text: In that day Jehovah, with his hard and great and strong sword, will turn his attention to Le·viʹa·than, the gliding serpent, even to Le·viʹa·than, the crooked serpent, and he will certainly kill the sea monster that is in the sea.

18269.label: Isaiah 27:2
18269.text: In that day sing to her, YOU people: “A vineyard of foaming wine!

18270.label: Isaiah 27:3
18270.text: I, Jehovah, am safeguarding her. Every moment I shall water her. In order that no one may turn his attention against her, I shall safeguard her even night and day.

18271.label: Isaiah 27:4
18271.text: There is no rage that I have. Who will give me thornbushes [and] weeds in the battle? I will step on such. I will set such on fire at the same time.

18272.label: Isaiah 27:5
18272.text: Otherwise let him take hold of my stronghold, let him make peace with me; peace let him make with me.”

18273.label: Isaiah 27:6
18273.text: In the coming [days] Jacob will take root, Israel will put forth blossoms and actually sprout; and they will simply fill the surface of the productive land with produce.

18274.label: Isaiah 27:7
18274.text: As with the stroke of one striking him does one have to strike him? Or as with the slaughter of his killed ones does he have to be killed?

18275.label: Isaiah 27:8
18275.text: With a scare cry you will contend with her when sending her forth. He must expel [her] with his blast, a hard one in the day of the east wind.

18276.label: Isaiah 27:9
18276.text: Therefore by this means the error of Jacob will be atoned for, and this is all the fruit [when] he takes away his sin, when he makes all the stones of the altar like chalkstones that have been pulverized, so that the sacred poles and the incense stands will not rise up.

18277.label: Isaiah 27:10
18277.text: For the fortified city will be solitary, the pasture ground will be left to itself and abandoned like a wilderness. There the calf will graze, and there it will lie down; and he will actually consume her boughs.

18278.label: Isaiah 27:11
18278.text: When her sprigs have dried up, women coming in will break [them] off, lighting them up. For it is not a people of keen understanding. That is why its Maker will show it no mercy, and its own Former will show it no favor.

18279.label: Isaiah 27:12
18279.text: And it must occur in that day that Jehovah will beat off [the fruit], from the flowing stream of the River to the torrent valley of Egypt, and so YOU yourselves will be picked up one after the other, O sons of Israel.

18280.label: Isaiah 27:13
18280.text: And it must occur in that day that there will be a blowing on a great horn, and those who are perishing in the land of As·syrʹi·a and those who are dispersed in the land of Egypt will certainly come and bow down to Jehovah in the holy mountain in Jerusalem.

18281.label: Isaiah 28:1
18281.text: Woe to the eminent crown of the drunkards of Eʹphra·im, and the fading blossom of its decoration of beauty that is upon the head of the fertile valley of those overpowered by wine!

18282.label: Isaiah 28:2
18282.text: Look! Jehovah has someone strong and vigorous. Like a thunderous storm of hail, a destructive storm, like a thunderous storm of powerful, flooding waters, he will certainly do a casting down to the earth with force.

18283.label: Isaiah 28:3
18283.text: With the feet the eminent crowns of the drunkards of Eʹphra·im will be trampled down.

18284.label: Isaiah 28:4
18284.text: And the fading flower of its decoration of beauty that is upon the head of the fertile valley must become like the early fig before summer, that, when the seer sees it, while it is yet in his palm, he swallows it down.

18285.label: Isaiah 28:5
18285.text: In that day Jehovah of armies will become as a crown of decoration and as a garland of beauty to the ones remaining over of his people,

18286.label: Isaiah 28:6
18286.text: and as a spirit of justice to the one sitting in the judgment, and as mightiness [to] those turning away the battle from the gate.

18287.label: Isaiah 28:7
18287.text: And these also—because of wine they have gone astray and because of intoxicating liquor they have wandered about. Priest and prophet —they have gone astray because of intoxicating liquor, they have become confused as a result of the wine, they have wandered about as a result of the intoxicating liquor; they have gone astray in their seeing, they have reeled as to decision.

18288.label: Isaiah 28:8
18288.text: For the tables themselves have all become full of filthy vomit —there is no place [without it].

18289.label: Isaiah 28:9
18289.text: Whom will one instruct in knowledge, and whom will one make understand what has been heard? Those who have been weaned from the milk, those moved away from the breasts?

18290.label: Isaiah 28:10
18290.text: For it is “command upon command, command upon command, measuring line upon measuring line, measuring line upon measuring line, here a little, there a little.”

18291.label: Isaiah 28:11
18291.text: For by those stammering with their lips and by a different tongue he will speak to this people,

18292.label: Isaiah 28:12
18292.text: those to whom he has said: “This is the resting-place. GIVE rest to the weary one. And this is the place of ease,” but who were not willing to hear.

18293.label: Isaiah 28:13
18293.text: And to them the word of Jehovah will certainly become “command upon command, command upon command, measuring line upon measuring line, measuring line upon measuring line, here a little, there a little,” in order that they may go and certainly stumble backwards and actually be broken and ensnared and caught.

18294.label: Isaiah 28:14
18294.text: Therefore hear the word of Jehovah, YOU braggarts, YOU rulers of this people who are in Jerusalem:

18295.label: Isaiah 28:15
18295.text: Because YOU men have said: “We have concluded a covenant with Death; and with Sheʹol we have effected a vision; the overflowing flash flood, in case it should pass through, will not come to us, for we have made a lie our refuge and in falsehood we have concealed ourselves”;

18296.label: Isaiah 28:16
18296.text: therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord Jehovah has said: “Here I am laying as a foundation in Zion a stone, a tried stone, the precious corner of a sure foundation. No one exercising faith will get panicky.

18297.label: Isaiah 28:17
18297.text: And I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the leveling instrument; and the hail must sweep away the refuge of a lie, and the waters themselves will flood out the very place of concealment.

18298.label: Isaiah 28:18
18298.text: And YOUR covenant with Death will certainly be dissolved, and that vision of YOURS with Sheʹol will not stand. The overflowing flash flood, when it passes through —YOU must also become for it a trampling place.

18299.label: Isaiah 28:19
18299.text: As often as it passes through, it will take YOU men away, because morning by morning it will pass through, during the day and during the night; and it must become nothing but a reason for quaking to make [others] understand what has been heard.”

18300.label: Isaiah 28:20
18300.text: For the couch has proved too short for stretching oneself on, and the woven sheet itself is [too] narrow when wrapping oneself up.

18301.label: Isaiah 28:21
18301.text: For Jehovah will rise up just as at Mount Pe·raʹzim, he will be agitated just as in the low plain near Gibʹe·on, that he may do his deed—his deed is strange—and that he may work his work —his work is unusual.

18302.label: Isaiah 28:22
18302.text: And now do not show yourselves scoffers, in order that YOUR bands may not grow strong, for there is an extermination, even something decided upon, that I have heard of from the Sovereign Lord, Jehovah of armies, for all the land.

18303.label: Isaiah 28:23
18303.text: Give ear, YOU men, and listen to my voice; pay attention and listen to my saying.

18304.label: Isaiah 28:24
18304.text: Is it all day long that the plower plows in order to sow seed, that he loosens and harrows his ground?

18305.label: Isaiah 28:25
18305.text: Does he not, when he has smoothed out its surface, then scatter black cumin and sprinkle the cumin, and must he not put in wheat, millet, and barley in the appointed place, and spelt as his boundary?

18306.label: Isaiah 28:26
18306.text: And one corrects him according to what is right. His own God instructs him.

18307.label: Isaiah 28:27
18307.text: For it is not with a threshing instrument that black cumin is given a treading; and upon cumin no wheel of a wagon is turned. For it is with a rod that black cumin is generally beaten out, and cumin with a staff.

18308.label: Isaiah 28:28
18308.text: Is breadstuff itself generally crushed? For never does one incessantly keep treading it out. And he must set the roller of his wagon in motion, and his own steeds, [but] he will not crush it.

18309.label: Isaiah 28:29
18309.text: This also is what has come forth from Jehovah of armies himself, who has been wonderful in counsel, who has done greatly in effectual working.

18310.label: Isaiah 29:1
18310.text: “Woe to Arʹi·el, to Arʹi·el, the town where David encamped! Add year upon year, YOU people; let the festivals run the round.

18311.label: Isaiah 29:2
18311.text: And I have to make things tight for Arʹi·el, and there must come to be mourning and lamentation, and she must become to me as the altar hearth of God.

18312.label: Isaiah 29:3
18312.text: And I must encamp on all sides against you, and I must lay siege to you with a palisade and raise up against you siegeworks.

18313.label: Isaiah 29:4
18313.text: And you must become low so that you will speak from the very earth, and as from the dust your saying will sound low. And like a spirit medium your voice must become even from the earth, and from the dust your own saying will chirp.

18314.label: Isaiah 29:5
18314.text: And the crowd of those strange to you must become just like fine powder, and the crowd of the tyrants just like the chaff that is passing away. And it must occur in an instant, suddenly.

18315.label: Isaiah 29:6
18315.text: From Jehovah of armies you will have attention with thunder and with quaking and with a great sound, storm wind and tempest, and the flame of a devouring fire.”

18316.label: Isaiah 29:7
18316.text: And it must occur just as in a dream, in a vision of the night, regarding the crowd of all the nations that are waging war against Arʹi·el, even all those waging war against her, and the siege towers against her and those making things tight for her.

18317.label: Isaiah 29:8
18317.text: Yes, it must occur just as when someone hungry dreams and here he is eating, and he actually awakes and his soul is empty; and just as when someone thirsty dreams and here he is drinking, and he actually awakes and here he is tired and his soul is dried out; thus it will occur with the crowd of all the nations that are waging war against Mount Zion.

18318.label: Isaiah 29:9
18318.text: Linger, YOU men, and be amazed; blind yourselves, and be blinded. They have become intoxicated, but not with wine; they have moved unsteadily, but not because of intoxicating liquor.

18319.label: Isaiah 29:10
18319.text: For upon YOU men Jehovah has poured a spirit of deep sleep; and he closes YOUR eyes, the prophets, and he has covered even YOUR heads, the visionaries.

18320.label: Isaiah 29:11
18320.text: And for YOU men the vision of everything becomes like the words of the book that has been sealed up, which they give to someone knowing the writing, saying: “Read this out loud, please,” and he has to say: “I am unable, for it is sealed up”;

18321.label: Isaiah 29:12
18321.text: and the book must be given to someone that does not know writing, [somebody] saying: “Read this out loud, please,” and he has to say: “I do not know writing at all.”

18322.label: Isaiah 29:13
18322.text: And Jehovah says: “For the reason that this people have come near with their mouth, and they have glorified me merely with their lips, and they have removed their heart itself far away from me, and their fear toward me becomes men’s commandment that is being taught,

18323.label: Isaiah 29:14
18323.text: therefore here I am, the One that will act wonderfully again with this people, in a wonderful manner and with something wonderful; and the wisdom of their wise men must perish, and the very understanding of their discreet men will conceal itself.”

18324.label: Isaiah 29:15
18324.text: Woe to those who are going very deep in concealing counsel from Jehovah himself, and whose deeds have occurred in a dark place, while they say: “Who is seeing us, and who is knowing of us?”

18325.label: Isaiah 29:16
18325.text: The perversity of YOU men! Should the potter himself be accounted just like the clay? For should the thing made say respecting its maker: “He did not make me”? And does the very thing formed actually say respecting its former: “He showed no understanding”?

18326.label: Isaiah 29:17
18326.text: Is it not yet but a very little time and Lebʹa·non must be turned into an orchard and the orchard itself will be accounted just as a forest?

18327.label: Isaiah 29:18
18327.text: And in that day the deaf ones will certainly hear the words of the book, and out of the gloom and out of the darkness even the eyes of the blind ones will see.

18328.label: Isaiah 29:19
18328.text: And the meek ones will certainly increase their rejoicing in Jehovah himself, and even the poor ones of mankind will be joyful in the Holy One of Israel himself,

18329.label: Isaiah 29:20
18329.text: because the tyrant must reach his end, and the bragger must come to his finish, and all those keeping alert to do harm must be cut off,

18330.label: Isaiah 29:21
18330.text: those bringing a man into sin by [his] word, and those who lay bait even for the one reproving in the gate, and those who push aside the righteous one with empty arguments.

18331.label: Isaiah 29:22
18331.text: Therefore this is what Jehovah has said to the house of Jacob, he that redeemed Abraham: “Jacob will not now be ashamed, nor will his own face now grow pale;

18332.label: Isaiah 29:23
18332.text: for when he sees his children, the work of my hands, in the midst of him, they will sanctify my name, and they will certainly sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and the God of Israel they will regard with awe.

18333.label: Isaiah 29:24
18333.text: And those who are erring in [their] spirit will actually get to know understanding, and even those who are grumbling will learn instruction.”

18334.label: Isaiah 30:1
18334.text: “Woe to the stubborn sons,” is the utterance of Jehovah, “[those disposed] to carry out counsel, but not that from me; and to pour out a libation, but not with my spirit, in order to add sin to sin;

18335.label: Isaiah 30:2
18335.text: those who are setting out to go down to Egypt and who have not inquired of my own mouth, to take shelter in the stronghold of Pharʹaoh and to take refuge in the shadow of Egypt!

18336.label: Isaiah 30:3
18336.text: And the stronghold of Pharʹaoh must become even for YOU men a reason for shame, and the refuge in the shadow of Egypt a cause for humiliation.

18337.label: Isaiah 30:4
18337.text: For his princes have come to be in Zoʹan itself, and his own envoys reach even Haʹnes.

18338.label: Isaiah 30:5
18338.text: Every one will certainly become ashamed of a people that bring no benefit to one, that are of no help and bring no benefit, but are a reason for shame and also a cause for reproach.”

18339.label: Isaiah 30:6
18339.text: The pronouncement against the beasts of the south: Through the land of distress and hard conditions, of the lion and the leopard growling, of the viper and the flying fiery snake, on the shoulders of full-grown asses they carry their resources, and on the humps of camels their supplies. In behalf of the people they will prove of no benefit.

18340.label: Isaiah 30:7
18340.text: And the Egyptians are mere vanity, and they will help simply for nothing. Therefore I have called this one: “Raʹhab —they are for sitting still.”

18341.label: Isaiah 30:8
18341.text: “Now come, write it upon a tablet with them, and inscribe it even in a book, that it may serve for a future day, for a witness to time indefinite.

18342.label: Isaiah 30:9
18342.text: For it is a rebellious people, untruthful sons, sons who have been unwilling to hear the law of Jehovah;

18343.label: Isaiah 30:10
18343.text: who have said to the ones seeing, ‘YOU must not see,’ and to the ones having visions, ‘YOU must not envision for us any straightforward things. Speak to us smooth things; envision deceptive things.

18344.label: Isaiah 30:11
18344.text: Turn aside from the way; deviate from the path. Cause the Holy One of Israel to cease just on account of us.’”

18345.label: Isaiah 30:12
18345.text: Therefore this is what the Holy One of Israel has said: “In view of YOUR rejecting of this word, and [since] YOU men trust in defrauding and in what is devious and YOU support yourselves on it,

18346.label: Isaiah 30:13
18346.text: therefore for YOU this error will become like a broken section about to fall down, a swelling out in a highly raised wall, the breakdown of which may come suddenly, in an instant.

18347.label: Isaiah 30:14
18347.text: And one will certainly break it as in the breaking of a large jar of the potters, crushed to pieces without one’s sparing [it], so that there cannot be found among its crushed pieces a fragment of earthenware with which to rake the fire from the fireplace or to skim water from a marshy place.”

18348.label: Isaiah 30:15
18348.text: For this is what the Sovereign Lord Jehovah, the Holy One of Israel, has said: “By coming back and resting YOU people will be saved. YOUR mightiness will prove to be simply in keeping undisturbed and in trustfulness.” But YOU were not willing.

18349.label: Isaiah 30:16
18349.text: And YOU proceeded to say: “No, but on horses we shall flee!” That is why YOU will flee. “And on swift [horses] we shall ride!” That is why those pursuing YOU will show themselves swift.

18350.label: Isaiah 30:17
18350.text: A thousand will tremble on account of the rebuke of one; on account of the rebuke of five YOU will flee until YOU will have remained over like a mast on the top of a mountain and like a signal on a hill.

18351.label: Isaiah 30:18
18351.text: And therefore Jehovah will keep in expectation of showing YOU favor, and therefore he will rise up to show YOU mercy. For Jehovah is a God of judgment. Happy are all those keeping in expectation of him.

18352.label: Isaiah 30:19
18352.text: When the very people in Zion will dwell in Jerusalem, you will by no means weep. He will without fail show you favor at the sound of your outcry; as soon as he hears it he will actually answer you.

18353.label: Isaiah 30:20
18353.text: And Jehovah will certainly give YOU people bread in the form of distress and water in the form of oppression; yet your Grand Instructor will no longer hide himself, and your eyes must become [eyes] seeing your Grand Instructor.

18354.label: Isaiah 30:21
18354.text: And your own ears will hear a word behind you saying: “This is the way. Walk in it, YOU people,” in case YOU people should go to the right or in case YOU should go to the left.

18355.label: Isaiah 30:22
18355.text: And YOU people must defile the overlaying of your graven images of silver and the close-fitting covering of your molten statue of gold. You will scatter them. Like a menstruating woman, you will say to it: “Mere dirt!”

18356.label: Isaiah 30:23
18356.text: And he will certainly give the rain for your seed with which you sow the ground, and as the produce of the ground bread, which must become fat and oily. Your livestock will graze in that day in a spacious pasture.

18357.label: Isaiah 30:24
18357.text: And the cattle and the full-grown asses cultivating the ground will eat fodder seasoned with sorrel, which was winnowed with the shovel and with the fork.

18358.label: Isaiah 30:25
18358.text: And upon every high mountain and upon every elevated hill there must come to be streams, water ditches, in the day of the big slaughter when the towers fall.

18359.label: Isaiah 30:26
18359.text: And the light of the full moon must become as the light of the glowing [sun]; and the very light of the glowing [sun] will become seven times as much, like the light of seven days, in the day that Jehovah binds up the breakdown of his people and heals even the severe wound resulting from the stroke by him.

18360.label: Isaiah 30:27
18360.text: Look! The name of Jehovah is coming from far away, burning with his anger and with heavy clouds. As for his lips, they have become full of denunciation, and his tongue is like a devouring fire.

18361.label: Isaiah 30:28
18361.text: And his spirit is like a flooding torrent that reaches clear to the neck, to swing the nations to and fro with a sieve of worthlessness; and a bridle that causes one to wander about will be in the jaws of the peoples.

18362.label: Isaiah 30:29
18362.text: YOU people will come to have a song like that in the night that one sanctifies oneself for a festival, and rejoicing of heart like that of one walking with a flute to enter into the mountain of Jehovah, to the Rock of Israel.

18363.label: Isaiah 30:30
18363.text: And Jehovah will certainly make the dignity of his voice to be heard and will make the descending of his arm to be seen, in the raging of anger and the flame of a devouring fire [and] cloudburst and rainstorm and hailstones.

18364.label: Isaiah 30:31
18364.text: For because of the voice of Jehovah As·syrʹi·a will be struck with terror; he will strike [it] even with a staff.

18365.label: Isaiah 30:32
18365.text: And every swing of his rod of chastisement that Jehovah will cause to settle down upon [As·syrʹi·a] will certainly prove to be with tambourines and with harps; and with battles of brandishing he will actually fight against them.

18366.label: Isaiah 30:33
18366.text: For his Toʹpheth is set in order from recent times; it is also prepared for the king himself. He has made its pile deep. Fire and wood are in abundance. The breath of Jehovah, like a torrent of sulphur, is burning against it.

18367.label: Isaiah 31:1
18367.text: Woe to those going down to Egypt for assistance, those who rely on mere horses, and who put their trust in war chariots, because they are numerous, and in steeds, because they are very mighty, but who have not looked to the Holy One of Israel and have not searched for Jehovah himself.

18368.label: Isaiah 31:2
18368.text: And he is also wise and will bring in what is calamitous, and he has not called back his own words; and he will certainly rise up against the house of evildoers and against the assistance of those practicing what is hurtful.

18369.label: Isaiah 31:3
18369.text: The Egyptians, though, are earthling men, and not God; and their horses are flesh, and not spirit. And Jehovah himself will stretch out his hand, and he that is offering help will have to stumble, and he that is being helped will have to fall, and at the same time they will all of them come to an end.

18370.label: Isaiah 31:4
18370.text: For this is what Jehovah has said to me: “Just as the lion growls, even the maned young lion, over its prey, when there is called out against it a full number of shepherds, [and] in spite of their voice he will not be terrified and in spite of their commotion he will not stoop; in the same way Jehovah of armies will come down to wage war over Mount Zion and over her hill.

18371.label: Isaiah 31:5
18371.text: Like birds flying, Jehovah of armies will in the same way defend Jerusalem. Defending [her], he will also certainly deliver [her]. Sparing [her], he must also cause [her] to escape.”

18372.label: Isaiah 31:6
18372.text: “Return, YOU people, to the One against whom the sons of Israel have gone deep in their revolt.

18373.label: Isaiah 31:7
18373.text: For in that day they will reject each one his worthless gods of silver and his valueless gods of gold, that YOUR hands have made for yourselves as a sin.

18374.label: Isaiah 31:8
18374.text: And the As·syrʹi·an must fall by the sword, not [that of] a man; and a sword, not [that of] earthling man, will devour him. And he must flee because of the sword, and his own young men will come to be for forced labor itself.

18375.label: Isaiah 31:9
18375.text: And his own crag will pass away out of sheer fright, and because of the signal his princes must be terrified,” is the utterance of Jehovah, whose light is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.

18376.label: Isaiah 32:1
18376.text: Look! A king will reign for righteousness itself; and as respects princes, they will rule as princes for justice itself.

18377.label: Isaiah 32:2
18377.text: And each one must prove to be like a hiding place from the wind and a place of concealment from the rainstorm, like streams of water in a waterless country, like the shadow of a heavy crag in an exhausted land.

18378.label: Isaiah 32:3
18378.text: And the eyes of those seeing will not be pasted together, and the very ears of those hearing will pay attention.

18379.label: Isaiah 32:4
18379.text: And the heart itself of those who are overhasty will consider knowledge, and even the tongue of the stammerers will be quick in speaking clear things.

18380.label: Isaiah 32:5
18380.text: The senseless one will no longer be called generous; and as for the unprincipled man, he will not be said to be noble;

18381.label: Isaiah 32:6
18381.text: because the senseless one himself will speak mere senselessness, and his very heart will work at what is hurtful, to work at apostasy and to speak against Jehovah what is wayward, to cause the soul of the hungry one to go empty, and he causes even the thirsty one to go without drink itself.

18382.label: Isaiah 32:7
18382.text: As for the unprincipled man, his instruments are bad; he himself has given counsel for acts of loose conduct, to wreck the afflicted ones with false sayings, even when someone poor speaks what is right.

18383.label: Isaiah 32:8
18383.text: As regards the generous one, it is for generous things that he has given counsel; and in favor of generous things he himself will rise up.

18384.label: Isaiah 32:9
18384.text: “YOU women who are at ease, rise up, listen to my voice! YOU careless daughters, give ear to my saying!

18385.label: Isaiah 32:10
18385.text: Within a year and some days YOU careless ones will be agitated, because the grape picking will have come to an end [but] no [fruit] gathering will come in.

18386.label: Isaiah 32:11
18386.text: Tremble, YOU women who are at ease! Be agitated, YOU careless ones! Undress and make yourselves naked, and gird [sackcloth] upon the loins.

18387.label: Isaiah 32:12
18387.text: Beat yourselves upon the breasts in lamentation over the desirable fields, over the fruit-bearing vine.

18388.label: Isaiah 32:13
18388.text: Upon the ground of my people merely thorns, spiny bushes come up, for they are upon all the houses of exultation, yes, the highly elated town.

18389.label: Isaiah 32:14
18389.text: For the dwelling tower itself has been forsaken, the very hubbub of the city has been abandoned; Oʹphel and the watchtower themselves have become bare fields, for time indefinite the exultation of zebras, the pasture of droves;

18390.label: Isaiah 32:15
18390.text: until upon us the spirit is poured out from on high, and the wilderness will have become an orchard, and the orchard itself is accounted as a real forest.

18391.label: Isaiah 32:16
18391.text: “And in the wilderness justice will certainly reside, and in the orchard righteousness itself will dwell.

18392.label: Isaiah 32:17
18392.text: And the work of the [true] righteousness must become peace; and the service of the [true] righteousness, quietness and security to time indefinite.

18393.label: Isaiah 32:18
18393.text: And my people must dwell in a peaceful abiding place and in residences of full confidence and in undisturbed resting-places.

18394.label: Isaiah 32:19
18394.text: And it will certainly hail when the forest goes down and the city becomes low in an abased state.

18395.label: Isaiah 32:20
18395.text: “Happy are YOU people who are sowing seed alongside all waters, sending forth the feet of the bull and of the ass.”

18396.label: Isaiah 33:1
18396.text: Woe to you who are despoiling, without you yourself being despoiled, and to you who are dealing treacherously, without [others] having dealt treacherously with you! As soon as you have finished as a despoiler, you will be despoiled. As soon as you have done with dealing treacherously, they will deal treacherously with you.

18397.label: Isaiah 33:2
18397.text: O Jehovah, show us favor. In you we have hoped. Become our arm every morning, yes, our salvation in the time of distress.

18398.label: Isaiah 33:3
18398.text: At the sound of turmoil peoples have fled. At your arising nations have been dispersed.

18399.label: Isaiah 33:4
18399.text: And the spoil of YOU people will actually be gathered [like] the cockroaches when gathering in, like the onrush of locust swarms that is rushing against one.

18400.label: Isaiah 33:5
18400.text: Jehovah will certainly be put on high, for he is residing in the height. He must fill Zion with justice and righteousness.

18401.label: Isaiah 33:6
18401.text: And the trustworthiness of your times must prove to be a wealth of salvations —wisdom and knowledge, the fear of Jehovah, which is his treasure.

18402.label: Isaiah 33:7
18402.text: Look! Their very heroes have cried out in the street; the very messengers of peace will weep bitterly.

18403.label: Isaiah 33:8
18403.text: The highways have been made desolate; the one passing over the path has ceased. He has broken the covenant; he has contemned the cities; he has taken no account of mortal man.

18404.label: Isaiah 33:9
18404.text: The land has gone mourning, has withered away. Lebʹa·non has become abashed; it has moldered. Sharʹon has become like the desert plain; and Baʹshan and Carʹmel are shaking off [their leaves].

18405.label: Isaiah 33:10
18405.text: “Now I will rise up,” says Jehovah, “now I will exalt myself; now I will lift myself up.

18406.label: Isaiah 33:11
18406.text: YOU people conceive dried grass; YOU will give birth to stubble. YOUR own spirit, as a fire, will eat YOU up.

18407.label: Isaiah 33:12
18407.text: And peoples must become as the burnings of lime. As thorns cut away, they will be set ablaze even with fire.

18408.label: Isaiah 33:13
18408.text: Hear, YOU men who are far away, what I must do! And know, YOU who are nearby, my mightiness.

18409.label: Isaiah 33:14
18409.text: In Zion the sinners have come to be in dread; shivering has grabbed hold of the apostates: ‘Who of us can reside for any time with a devouring fire? Who of us can reside for any time with long-lasting conflagrations?’

18410.label: Isaiah 33:15
18410.text: “There is one who is walking in continual righteousness and speaking what is upright, who is rejecting the unjust gain from frauds, who is shaking his hands clear from taking hold on a bribe, who is stopping up his ear from listening to bloodshed, and who is closing his eyes so as not to see what is bad.

18411.label: Isaiah 33:16
18411.text: He is the one that will reside on the heights themselves; his secure height will be craggy places difficult to approach. His own bread will certainly be given [him]; his water supply will be unfailing.”

18412.label: Isaiah 33:17
18412.text: A king in his handsomeness is what your eyes will behold; they will see a land far away.

18413.label: Isaiah 33:18
18413.text: Your own heart will comment in low tones on a frightful thing: “Where is the secretary? Where is the one that does the paying out? Where is the one counting the towers?”

18414.label: Isaiah 33:19
18414.text: No insolent people will you see, a people too deep in language to listen to, of a stammering tongue without [your] understanding.

18415.label: Isaiah 33:20
18415.text: Behold Zion, the town of our festal occasions! Your own eyes will see Jerusalem an undisturbed abiding place, a tent that no one will pack up. Never will its tent pins be pulled out, and none of its ropes will be torn in two.

18416.label: Isaiah 33:21
18416.text: But there the Majestic One, Jehovah, will be for us a place of rivers, of wide canals. On it no galley fleet will go, and no majestic ship will pass over it.

18417.label: Isaiah 33:22
18417.text: For Jehovah is our Judge, Jehovah is our Statute-giver, Jehovah is our King; he himself will save us.

18418.label: Isaiah 33:23
18418.text: Your ropes must hang loose; their mast they will not hold firmly erect; they have not spread a sail. At that time even spoil in abundance will have to be divided up; the lame ones themselves will actually take a big plunder.

18419.label: Isaiah 33:24
18419.text: And no resident will say: “I am sick.” The people that are dwelling in [the land] will be those pardoned for their error.

18420.label: Isaiah 34:1
18420.text: Come up close, YOU nations, to hear; and YOU national groups, pay attention. Let the earth and that which fills it listen, the productive land and all its produce.

18421.label: Isaiah 34:2
18421.text: For Jehovah has indignation against all the nations, and rage against all their army. He must devote them to destruction; he must give them to the slaughter.

18422.label: Isaiah 34:3
18422.text: And their slain ones will be thrown out; and as for their carcasses, their stink will ascend; and the mountains must melt because of their blood.

18423.label: Isaiah 34:4
18423.text: And all those of the army of the heavens must rot away. And the heavens must be rolled up, just like a book scroll; and their army will all shrivel away, just as the leafage shrivels off the vine and like a shriveled [fig] off the fig tree.

18424.label: Isaiah 34:5
18424.text: “For in the heavens my sword will certainly be drenched. Look! Upon Eʹdom it will descend, and upon the people devoted by me to destruction in justice.

18425.label: Isaiah 34:6
18425.text: Jehovah has a sword; it must be filled with blood; it must be made greasy with the fat, with the blood of young rams and he-goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams. For Jehovah has a sacrifice in Bozʹrah, and a great slaughtering in the land of Eʹdom.

18426.label: Isaiah 34:7
18426.text: And the wild bulls must come down with them, and young bulls with the powerful ones; and their land must be drenched with blood, and their very dust will be made greasy with the fat.”

18427.label: Isaiah 34:8
18427.text: For Jehovah has a day of vengeance, a year of retributions for the legal case over Zion.

18428.label: Isaiah 34:9
18428.text: And her torrents must be changed into pitch, and her dust into sulphur; and her land must become as burning pitch.

18429.label: Isaiah 34:10
18429.text: By night or by day it will not be extinguished; to time indefinite its smoke will keep ascending. From generation to generation she will be parched; forever and ever no one will be passing across her.

18430.label: Isaiah 34:11
18430.text: And the pelican and the porcupine must take possession of her, and long-eared owls and ravens themselves will reside in her; and he must stretch out over her the measuring line of emptiness and the stones of wasteness.

18431.label: Isaiah 34:12
18431.text: Her nobles—there are none there whom they will call to the kingship itself, and her very princes will all become nothing.

18432.label: Isaiah 34:13
18432.text: On her dwelling towers thorns must come up, nettles and thorny weeds in her fortified places; and she must become an abiding place of jackals, the courtyard for the ostriches.

18433.label: Isaiah 34:14
18433.text: And haunters of waterless regions must meet up with howling animals, and even the goat-shaped demon will call to its companion. Yes, there the nightjar will certainly take its ease and find for itself a resting-place.

18434.label: Isaiah 34:15
18434.text: There the arrow snake has made its nest and lays [eggs], and it must hatch [them] and gather [them] together under its shadow. Yes, there the gledes must collect themselves together, each one with her mate.

18435.label: Isaiah 34:16
18435.text: Search for yourselves in the book of Jehovah and read out loud: not one has been missing of them; they actually do not fail to have each one her mate, for it is the mouth of Jehovah that has given the command, and it is his spirit that has collected them together.

18436.label: Isaiah 34:17
18436.text: And it is He that has cast for them the lot, and his own hand has apportioned the place to them by the measuring line. To time indefinite they will take possession of it; for generation after generation they will reside in it.

18437.label: Isaiah 35:1
18437.text: The wilderness and the waterless region will exult, and the desert plain will be joyful and blossom as the saffron.

18438.label: Isaiah 35:2
18438.text: Without fail it will blossom, and it will really be joyful with joyousness and with glad crying out. The glory of Lebʹa·non itself must be given to it, the splendor of Carʹmel and of Sharʹon. There will be those who will see the glory of Jehovah, the splendor of our God.

18439.label: Isaiah 35:3
18439.text: Strengthen the weak hands, YOU people, and make the knees that are wobbling firm.

18440.label: Isaiah 35:4
18440.text: Say to those who are anxious at heart: “Be strong. Do not be afraid. Look! YOUR own God will come with vengeance itself, God even with a repayment. He himself will come and save YOU people.”

18441.label: Isaiah 35:5
18441.text: At that time the eyes of the blind ones will be opened, and the very ears of the deaf ones will be unstopped.

18442.label: Isaiah 35:6
18442.text: At that time the lame one will climb up just as a stag does, and the tongue of the speechless one will cry out in gladness. For in the wilderness waters will have burst out, and torrents in the desert plain.

18443.label: Isaiah 35:7
18443.text: And the heat-parched ground will have become as a reedy pool, and the thirsty ground as springs of water. In the abiding place of jackals, a resting-place for [them], there will be green grass with reeds and papyrus plants.

18444.label: Isaiah 35:8
18444.text: And there will certainly come to be a highway there, even a way; and the Way of Holiness it will be called. The unclean one will not pass over it. And it will be for the one walking on the way, and no foolish ones will wander about [on it].

18445.label: Isaiah 35:9
18445.text: No lion will prove to be there, and the rapacious sort of wild beasts will not come up on it. None will be found there; and the repurchased ones must walk [there].

18446.label: Isaiah 35:10
18446.text: And the very ones redeemed by Jehovah will return and certainly come to Zion with a joyful cry; and rejoicing to time indefinite will be upon their head. To exultation and rejoicing they will attain, and grief and sighing must flee away.

18447.label: Isaiah 36:1
18447.text: Now it came about in the fourteenth year of King Hez·e·kiʹah that Sen·nachʹer·ib the king of As·syrʹi·a came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and proceeded to seize them.

18448.label: Isaiah 36:2
18448.text: And the king of As·syrʹi·a finally sent Rabʹsha·keh from Laʹchish to Jerusalem, to King Hez·e·kiʹah, with a heavy military force, and he proceeded to stand still by the conduit of the upper pool at the highway of the laundryman’s field.

18449.label: Isaiah 36:3
18449.text: Then there came out to him E·liʹa·kim the son of Hil·kiʹah, who was over the household, and Shebʹna the secretary and Joʹah the son of Aʹsaph the recorder.

18450.label: Isaiah 36:4
18450.text: Accordingly Rabʹsha·keh said to them: “Please, say to Hez·e·kiʹah, ‘This is what the great king, the king of As·syrʹi·a, has said: “What is this confidence in which you have trusted?

18451.label: Isaiah 36:5
18451.text: You have said (but it is the word of lips), ‘There are counsel and mightiness for the war.’ Now in whom have you put trust, that you have rebelled against me?

18452.label: Isaiah 36:6
18452.text: Look! You have trusted in the support of this crushed reed, in Egypt, which, if a man should brace himself upon it, would certainly enter into his palm and pierce it. That is the way Pharʹaoh the king of Egypt is to all those putting their trust in him.

18453.label: Isaiah 36:7
18453.text: And in case you should say to me, ‘It is Jehovah our God in whom we have trusted,’ is he not the one whose high places and whose altars Hez·e·kiʹah has removed, while he says to Judah and Jerusalem, ‘Before this altar YOU should bow down’?”’

18454.label: Isaiah 36:8
18454.text: Now, then, make a wager, please, with my lord the king of As·syrʹi·a, and let me give you two thousand horses [to see] whether you are able, on your part, to put riders upon them.

18455.label: Isaiah 36:9
18455.text: How, then, could you turn back the face of one governor of the smallest servants of my lord, while you, for your part, put your trust in Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?

18456.label: Isaiah 36:10
18456.text: And now is it without authorization from Jehovah that I have come up against this land to bring it to ruin? Jehovah himself said to me, ‘Go up against this land, and you must bring it to ruin.’”

18457.label: Isaiah 36:11
18457.text: At this E·liʹa·kim and Shebʹna and Joʹah said to Rabʹsha·keh: “Speak, please, to your servants in the Syrian language, for we are listening; and do not speak to us in the Jews’ language in the ears of the people that are on the wall.”

18458.label: Isaiah 36:12
18458.text: But Rabʹsha·keh said: “Is it to your lord and to you that my lord has sent me to speak these words? Is it not to the men sitting upon the wall, that they may eat their own excrement and drink their own urine with YOU men?”

18459.label: Isaiah 36:13
18459.text: And Rabʹsha·keh continued to stand and call out in a loud voice in the Jews’ language, and he went on to say: “HEAR the words of the great king, the king of As·syrʹi·a.

18460.label: Isaiah 36:14
18460.text: This is what the king has said, ‘Do not let Hez·e·kiʹah deceive YOU people, for he is not able to deliver YOU.

18461.label: Isaiah 36:15
18461.text: And do not let Hez·e·kiʹah cause YOU to trust in Jehovah, saying: “Without fail Jehovah will deliver us. This city will not be given into the hand of the king of As·syrʹi·a.”

18462.label: Isaiah 36:16
18462.text: Do not listen to Hez·e·kiʹah, for this is what the king of As·syrʹi·a has said: “Make a capitulation to me and come out to me and eat each one from his own vine and each one from his own fig tree and drink each one the water of his own cistern,

18463.label: Isaiah 36:17
18463.text: until I come and actually take YOU to a land like YOUR own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards;

18464.label: Isaiah 36:18
18464.text: in order that Hez·e·kiʹah may not allure YOU, saying, ‘Jehovah himself will deliver us.’ Have the gods of the nations delivered each one his own land out of the hand of the king of As·syrʹi·a?

18465.label: Isaiah 36:19
18465.text: Where are the gods of Haʹmath and Arʹpad? Where are the gods of Seph·ar·vaʹim? And have they delivered Sa·marʹi·a out of my hand?

18466.label: Isaiah 36:20
18466.text: Who are there among all the gods of these lands that have delivered their land out of my hand so that Jehovah should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?”’”

18467.label: Isaiah 36:21
18467.text: And they continued to keep silent and did not answer him a word, for the commandment of the king was, saying: “YOU must not answer him.”

18468.label: Isaiah 36:22
18468.text: But E·liʹa·kim the son of Hil·kiʹah, who was over the household, and Shebʹna the secretary and Joʹah the son of Aʹsaph the recorder came to Hez·e·kiʹah with their garments ripped apart, and told him the words of Rabʹsha·keh.

18469.label: Isaiah 37:1
18469.text: And it came about that as soon as King Hez·e·kiʹah heard, he immediately ripped his garments apart and covered himself with sackcloth and came into the house of Jehovah.

18470.label: Isaiah 37:2
18470.text: Further, he sent E·liʹa·kim, who was over the household, and Shebʹna the secretary and the older men of the priests covered with sackcloth to Isaiah the son of Aʹmoz the prophet.

18471.label: Isaiah 37:3
18471.text: And they proceeded to say to him: “This is what Hez·e·kiʹah has said, ‘This day is a day of distress and of rebuke and of scornful insolence, for the sons have come as far as the womb’s mouth, and there is no power to give birth.

18472.label: Isaiah 37:4
18472.text: Perhaps Jehovah your God will hear the words of Rabʹsha·keh, whom the king of As·syrʹi·a his lord sent to taunt the living God, and he will actually call him to account for the words that Jehovah your God has heard. And you must lift up prayer in behalf of the remnant that are to be found.’”

18473.label: Isaiah 37:5
18473.text: So the servants of King Hez·e·kiʹah came in to Isaiah.

18474.label: Isaiah 37:6
18474.text: Then Isaiah said to them: “This is what YOU should say to YOUR lord, ‘This is what Jehovah has said: “Do not be afraid because of the words that you have heard with which the attendants of the king of As·syrʹi·a spoke abusively of me.

18475.label: Isaiah 37:7
18475.text: Here I am putting a spirit in him, and he must hear a report and return to his own land; and I shall certainly cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.”’”

18476.label: Isaiah 37:8
18476.text: After that Rabʹsha·keh returned and found the king of As·syrʹi·a fighting against Libʹnah, for he had heard that he had pulled away from Laʹchish.

18477.label: Isaiah 37:9
18477.text: Now he heard it said concerning Tir·haʹkah the king of E·thi·oʹpi·a: “He has come out to fight against you.” When he heard, he at once sent messengers to Hez·e·kiʹah, saying:

18478.label: Isaiah 37:10
18478.text: “This is what YOU men should say to Hez·e·kiʹah the king of Judah, ‘Do not let your God in whom you are trusting deceive you, saying: “Jerusalem will not be given into the hand of the king of As·syrʹi·a.”

18479.label: Isaiah 37:11
18479.text: Look! You yourself have heard what the kings of As·syrʹi·a did to all the lands by devoting them to destruction, and will you yourself be delivered?

18480.label: Isaiah 37:12
18480.text: Have the gods of the nations that my forefathers brought to ruin delivered them, even Goʹzan and Haʹran and Reʹzeph and the sons of Eʹden that were in Tel-asʹsar?

18481.label: Isaiah 37:13
18481.text: Where is the king of Haʹmath and the king of Arʹpad and the king of the city of Seph·ar·vaʹim —of Heʹna and of Ivʹvah?’”

18482.label: Isaiah 37:14
18482.text: Then Hez·e·kiʹah took the letters out of the hand of the messengers and read them, after which Hez·e·kiʹah went up to the house of Jehovah and spread it out before Jehovah.

18483.label: Isaiah 37:15
18483.text: And Hez·e·kiʹah began to pray to Jehovah, saying:

18484.label: Isaiah 37:16
18484.text: “O Jehovah of armies, the God of Israel, sitting upon the cherubs, you alone are the [true] God of all the kingdoms of the earth. You yourself have made the heavens and the earth.

18485.label: Isaiah 37:17
18485.text: Incline your ear, O Jehovah, and hear. Open your eyes, O Jehovah, and see, and hear all the words of Sen·nachʹer·ib that he has sent to taunt the living God.

18486.label: Isaiah 37:18
18486.text: It is a fact, O Jehovah, that the kings of As·syrʹi·a have devastated all the lands, and their own land.

18487.label: Isaiah 37:19
18487.text: And there was a consigning of their gods to the fire, because they were no gods, but the workmanship of man’s hands, wood and stone, so that they destroyed them.

18488.label: Isaiah 37:20
18488.text: And now, O Jehovah our God, save us out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you, O Jehovah, are [God] alone.”

18489.label: Isaiah 37:21
18489.text: And Isaiah the son of Aʹmoz proceeded to send to Hez·e·kiʹah, saying: “This is what Jehovah the God of Israel has said, ‘Because you have prayed to me concerning Sen·nachʹer·ib the king of As·syrʹi·a,

18490.label: Isaiah 37:22
18490.text: this is the word that Jehovah has spoken against him: “The virgin daughter of Zion has despised you, she has held you in derision. Behind you the daughter of Jerusalem has wagged [her] head.

18491.label: Isaiah 37:23
18491.text: Whom have you taunted and spoken of abusively? And against whom have you lifted up [your] voice And do you raise your eyes on high? It is against the Holy One of Israel!

18492.label: Isaiah 37:24
18492.text: By means of your servants you have taunted Jehovah and you say, ‘With the multitude of my war chariots I myself —I shall certainly ascend the height of mountainous regions, The remotest parts of Lebʹa·non; And I shall cut down its lofty cedars, its choice juniper trees. And I shall enter its final height, the forest of its orchard.

18493.label: Isaiah 37:25
18493.text: I myself shall certainly dig and drink waters,And I shall dry up with the soles of my feet all the Nile canals of Egypt.’

18494.label: Isaiah 37:26
18494.text: Have you not heard? From remote times it is what I will do. From bygone days I have even formed it. Now I will bring it in. And you will serve to make fortified cities become desolate as piles of ruins.

18495.label: Isaiah 37:27
18495.text: And their inhabitants will be feeble-handed; They will simply be terrified and ashamed. They must become as vegetation of the field and green tender grass, Grass of the roofs and of the terrace before the east wind.

18496.label: Isaiah 37:28
18496.text: And your sitting quiet and your going out and your coming in I well know, And your exciting yourself against me,

18497.label: Isaiah 37:29
18497.text: Because your exciting yourself against me and your roaring have come up into my ears. And I shall certainly put my hook in your nose and my bridle between your lips, And I shall indeed lead you back by the way by which you have come.”

18498.label: Isaiah 37:30
18498.text: “‘And this will be the sign for you: There will be an eating this year of the growth from spilled kernels, and in the second year grain that shoots up of itself; but in the third year sow seed, YOU people, and reap, and plant vineyards and eat their fruitage.

18499.label: Isaiah 37:31
18499.text: And those who escape of the house of Judah, those who are left remaining, will certainly take root downward and produce fruitage upward.

18500.label: Isaiah 37:32
18500.text: For out of Jerusalem a remnant will go forth and those who escape out of Mount Zion. The very zeal of Jehovah of armies will do this.

18501.label: Isaiah 37:33
18501.text: “‘Therefore this is what Jehovah has said concerning the king of As·syrʹi·a: “He will not come into this city, nor will he shoot an arrow there, nor confront it with a shield, nor cast up a siege rampart against it.”’

18502.label: Isaiah 37:34
18502.text: “‘By the way by which he came he will return, and into this city he will not come,’ is the utterance of Jehovah.

18503.label: Isaiah 37:35
18503.text: ‘And I shall certainly defend this city to save it for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant.’”

18504.label: Isaiah 37:36
18504.text: And the angel of Jehovah proceeded to go forth and strike down a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the camp of the As·syrʹi·ans. When people rose up early in the morning, why, there all of them were dead carcasses.

18505.label: Isaiah 37:37
18505.text: Hence Sen·nachʹer·ib the king of As·syrʹi·a pulled away and went and returned and took up dwelling in Ninʹe·veh.

18506.label: Isaiah 37:38
18506.text: And it came about that as he was bowing down at the house of Nisʹroch his god, A·dramʹme·lech and Shar·eʹzer, his own sons, struck him down with the sword, and they themselves escaped to the land of Arʹa·rat. And Eʹsar-hadʹdon his son began to reign in place of him.

18507.label: Isaiah 38:1
18507.text: In those days Hez·e·kiʹah got sick to the point of dying. Accordingly Isaiah the son of Aʹmoz the prophet came in to him and said to him: “This is what Jehovah has said, ‘Give commands to your household, for you yourself will indeed die and will not live.’”

18508.label: Isaiah 38:2
18508.text: At that Hez·e·kiʹah turned his face to the wall and began to pray to Jehovah

18509.label: Isaiah 38:3
18509.text: and to say: “I beseech you, O Jehovah, remember, please, how I have walked before you in truthfulness and with a complete heart, and what was good in your eyes I have done.” And Hez·e·kiʹah began to weep profusely.

18510.label: Isaiah 38:4
18510.text: And the word of Jehovah now occurred to Isaiah, saying:

18511.label: Isaiah 38:5
18511.text: “Go, and you must say to Hez·e·kiʹah, ‘This is what Jehovah the God of David your forefather has said: “I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. Here I am adding onto your days fifteen years;

18512.label: Isaiah 38:6
18512.text: and out of the palm of the king of As·syrʹi·a I shall deliver you and this city, and I will defend this city.

18513.label: Isaiah 38:7
18513.text: And this is the sign for you from Jehovah that Jehovah will perform this word that he has spoken:

18514.label: Isaiah 38:8
18514.text: Here I am making the shadow of the steps that had gone down on the steps [of the stairs] of Aʹhaz by the sun retrace backward ten steps.”’” And the sun gradually went back ten steps on the steps [of the stairs] that it had gone down.

18515.label: Isaiah 38:9
18515.text: A writing of Hez·e·kiʹah the king of Judah, when he got sick and revived from his sickness.

18516.label: Isaiah 38:10
18516.text: I myself said: “In the midst of my days I will go into the gates of Sheʹol.I must be deprived of the remainder of my years.”

18517.label: Isaiah 38:11
18517.text: I have said: “I shall not see Jah, even Jah, in the land of the living ones. I shall no more look on mankind —with the inhabitants of [the land of] cessation.

18518.label: Isaiah 38:12
18518.text: My own habitation has been pulled out and removed from me like the tent of shepherds. I have rolled up my life just like a loom worker;One proceeds to cut me off from the very threads of the warp. From daylight till night you keep handing me over.

18519.label: Isaiah 38:13
18519.text: I have soothed myself until the morning. Like a lion, so he keeps breaking all my bones; From daylight till night you keep handing me over.

18520.label: Isaiah 38:14
18520.text: Like the swift, the bulbul, so I keep chirping; I keep cooing like the dove. My eyes have looked languishingly to the height: ‘O Jehovah, I am under oppression. Stand good for me.’

18521.label: Isaiah 38:15
18521.text: What shall I speak, and [what] will he actually say to me? He himself has also acted. I keep walking solemnly all my years in the bitterness of my soul.

18522.label: Isaiah 38:16
18522.text: ‘O Jehovah, on that account they keep living; and as with everybody, thereby is the life of my spirit. And you will restore me to health and certainly preserve me alive.

18523.label: Isaiah 38:17
18523.text: Look! For peace I had what was bitter, yes, bitter; And you yourself have become attached to my soul [and kept it] from the pit of disintegration. For you have thrown behind your back all my sins.

18524.label: Isaiah 38:18
18524.text: For it is not Sheʹol that can laud you; death itself cannot praise you. Those going down into the pit cannot look hopefully to your trueness.

18525.label: Isaiah 38:19
18525.text: The living, the living, he is the one that can laud you, Just as I can this day. The father himself can give knowledge to his own sons concerning your trueness.

18526.label: Isaiah 38:20
18526.text: O Jehovah, [undertake] to save me, and we shall play my string selections All the days of our life at the house of Jehovah.’”

18527.label: Isaiah 38:21
18527.text: And Isaiah proceeded to say: “Let them take a cake of pressed dried figs and rub [it] in upon the boil, that he may revive.”

18528.label: Isaiah 38:22
18528.text: Meantime, Hez·e·kiʹah said: “What is the sign that I shall go up to the house of Jehovah?”

18529.label: Isaiah 39:1
18529.text: At that time Merʹo·dach-balʹa·dan the son of Balʹa·dan the king of Babylon sent letters and a gift to Hez·e·kiʹah, after he heard that he had been sick but was strong again.

18530.label: Isaiah 39:2
18530.text: So Hez·e·kiʹah began to rejoice over them and proceeded to show them his treasure-house, the silver and the gold and the balsam oil and the good oil and all his armory and all that was to be found in his treasures. There proved to be nothing that Hez·e·kiʹah did not show them in his own house and in all his dominion.

18531.label: Isaiah 39:3
18531.text: After that Isaiah the prophet came in to King Hez·e·kiʹah and said to him: “What did these men say, and from where did they proceed to come to you?” So Hez·e·kiʹah said: “From a distant land they came to me, from Babylon.”

18532.label: Isaiah 39:4
18532.text: And he went on to say: “What did they see in your house?” To this Hez·e·kiʹah said: “Everything that is in my house they saw. There proved to be nothing that I did not show them in my treasures.”

18533.label: Isaiah 39:5
18533.text: Isaiah now said to Hez·e·kiʹah: “Hear the word of Jehovah of armies,

18534.label: Isaiah 39:6
18534.text: ‘Look! Days are coming, and all that is in your own house and that your forefathers have stored up down to this day will actually be carried to Babylon.’ ‘Nothing will be left,’ Jehovah has said.

18535.label: Isaiah 39:7
18535.text: ‘And some of your own sons that will come forth from you, to whom you will become father, will themselves be taken and actually become court officials in the palace of the king of Babylon.’”

18536.label: Isaiah 39:8
18536.text: At that Hez·e·kiʹah said to Isaiah: “The word of Jehovah that you have spoken is good.” And he went on to say: “Because peace and truth will continue in my own days.”

18537.label: Isaiah 40:1
